description: Open-source YAML policy engine written in Rust that acts as a transparent stdio proxy between AI agents and MCP servers, evaluating every tool call before execution with fail-closed enforcement.
agents: Not an agent deployer — they ARE the enforcement layer for any AI agent using MCP servers
Target users: devs running Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any agent with MCP tool access
Policies cover: Postgres (DROP TABLE gates), GitHub (force-push gates), Slack (send gates), Shell (rm -rf blocks)

funding.notes: Solo indie developer. No company, no VC. Just launched via HN Show HN (item 47255351). 128+ policy tests, 8 server policy templates.

pp_fit.feature: Complementary enforcement layer — Kvlar blocks/gates, PP provides the authorization receipts for what got approved
actions_needing_receipts: tool_call_execution (any MCP action that was allowed)
pp_fit.integration_complexity: low — PP SDK wraps the 'allow' decisions and issues receipts; Kvlar handles enforcement
pp_fit.urgency: low — open-source project, no enterprise urgency
pp_fit.differentiation: Kvlar = enforcement (what CAN happen). PP = receipts (proof of WHAT DID happen and who authorized it). Different layers, potentially stackable. Kvlar has zero audit trail, no tamper-evident receipts, no enterprise compliance capability. PP fills that gap.
pp_fit.opportunity: Ally/integration play. If Kvlar gains traction in dev community, PP could integrate as the audit receipt layer on top. Or Kvlar developer could become an advocate.

notes: Too early for outreach — solo dev, unfunded. Monitor GitHub repo growth and HN traction. If Kvlar gets meaningful stars/adoption, reach out to propose PP as audit receipt layer on top of their enforcement engine. High conceptual alignment, zero business leverage today.
